note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Prepare statements run in one PowerShell session with the episode folder as current directory; variables do not survive into the screens, so each screen re-derives what it needs.
prepare: Push-Location C:\demo\mg-commit; npm ci --no-audit --no-fund; npm run compile; Pop-Location
git config user.name 'Alex Demo'; git config user.email 'alex.demo@contoso.com'
git add .; git commit -q -m 'chore: add repo guardrails'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force src | Out-Null; 'PAGE_SIZE = 50' | Set-Content src/orders.py; git add src/orders.py
# the profile 'DevTools Demo' is created empty by the first `code --profile` call in the first screen

screens.name: recommended
steps: In Windows Terminal run: code --profile "DevTools Demo" C:\demo\team-setup   (the profile does not exist yet, VS Code creates it empty)
Wait for the notification bottom right: 'Do you want to install the recommended extensions for this repository?' and keep it in frame
Open the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X), type @recommended in the search box
Show the WORKSPACE RECOMMENDATIONS group with the seven extensions from .vscode/extensions.json; do not click Install if it would take long
mask: Windows user name in the title bar and paths (the folder is under C:\demo)
Accounts icon / Settings Sync badge at the bottom of the activity bar

screens.name: validate
steps: Open C:\demo\mg-commit in VS Code and press F5 (Run Extension)
In the Extension Development Host open the folder C:\demo\orders-app
Source Control view: click the pencil icon in the title bar (or Command Palette > MG: Compose Conventional Commit)
Pick type feat, scope orders, breaking change No
In the subject box type: Added paging.   and capture the red message 'Start with a lower-case verb: add, fix, remove...'
Clear it and type a long subject (more than about 65 characters) and capture 'Header is 7x/72 characters: shorten the subject'
mask: Windows user name in the title bar and paths

screens.name: commitbox
steps: In the Source Control commit box type: line 1 'wip', line 2 empty, line 3 'Uses cursor paging.'
Run MG: Compose Conventional Commit with feat, orders, No, subject: add paging
Capture the commit box: 'feat(orders): add paging', blank line, 'Uses cursor paging.'
Press Ctrl+Enter to commit; the episode 1 commit-msg hook accepts it
Open the integrated terminal and run: git log --oneline -1   and capture the commit
mask: Windows user name in the terminal prompt and title bar (use a short prompt)
screens.note: Optional check from demo.md: in a multi-root workspace with two repos the pencil in each repository's title bar fills that repo's commit box.

teardown: # owner: VS Code > Profiles editor > delete 'DevTools Demo' (profiles cannot be removed from the command line)
